African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, has said Nigerians may no longer need to build security fences around their homes if he becomes president. He promised to tackle insecurity through technology-driven measures, including the deployment of drones and artificial intelligence. He said his proposed approach to security would create an environment where Nigerians could move freely, cultivate their land and live without fear of attacks by criminals. Sowore made the remarks while interacting with journalists in Asaba, Delta State, on Saturday, during his #RevolutionExpress campaign visit. He said his administration would prioritise the use of technology to identify criminal elements and prevent attacks before they occurred, rather than rely on conventional security arrangements such as roadblocks. “Full security means nobody will go hungry in our time because we make our land, you know, free to cultivate once again by providing security for everyone in the country. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Security that is driven by technology, no more outside security of roadblocks. Drones, AI, to help us figure out where the criminals are, we bust them before they get to our people,” he said. The AAC candidate said improved security and responsible leadership would also reduce the need for elaborate security barriers around residential buildings. “So, if you vote right, you may not need fence in your houses anymore, except you will need it to decorate,” he added. He said he had lived in a society for 20 years where even wealthy people did not surround their homes with fences, using the experience to illustrate the level of public safety he hoped to achieve in Nigeria. Tinubu arrives Lagos after Ibadan APC rally 2027: Tinubu endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat at Ibadan rally Akpabio asks APC to shun violence Sowore also criticised the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government, dismissing its reforms and accusing the ruling party of failing to develop a workable plan for the country. Asked whether the APC’s reforms were working, he said, “APC, don’t be messing with me. APC is on its way out. There was no time they had any plan for the country. They lied to Nigerians in 2015 and their lives are caught up with that.” He further accused the ruling party of hiring crowds for its political activities across the country, alleging that it continued to mislead Nigerians. “That’s why they have to be hiring crowds, you know, all around the country and they keep lying,” he added. Sowore arrived in Asaba on Thursday evening for a campaign stop and held a press conference upon arrival. His visit formed part of his political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. The latest promise is consistent with his previous advocacy for technology-driven security. In an earlier interview, the activist-turned-politician said he would make a drone his defence minister if elected president, arguing that Nigeria needed to embrace technology to improve its security operations. He had also advocated the use of drones and modern surveillance systems to monitor criminal activities , gather intelligence and enable security agencies to respond to threats more effectively. Sowore has also made proposals on education as part of his campaign promises. He recently pledged to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students in tertiary institutions. The presidential candidate has continued to make security, governance, education and economic reforms central to his campaign messaging ahead of the 2027 elections.
